lines: The app ships no composer/autoload.php, so the server registers its generic loader for lib/ and looks every class up in the file system.

A composer/composer.json with config.vendor-dir ".", config.optimize-autoloader true, a config.autoloader-suffix and autoload.psr-4 {"OCA\\CertexiSync\\": "../lib/"} makes composer dump-autoload write composer/autoload.php with a class map; the code of the app does not change.

1 transaction is opened and closed by hand. The trait TTransactional has atomic() since Nextcloud 24 and atomicRetry() since Nextcloud 27, which repeats a transaction that ran into a deadlock, as the manual recommends.
lib/Controller/ApiController.php:139

The app reads and writes its app config in 2 places and registers no config lexicon, which IRegistrationContext::registerConfigLexicon() takes since Nextcloud 31. A lexicon states the type, the default and the sensitivity of each key in one place.
lib/Service/Journal.php:56 getValueInt()
lib/Service/Journal.php:97 setValueInt()
Nothing in the app calls 3 OCS routes. OCS is there for clients outside the app, so this is no defect in itself.
GET /ocs/v2.php/apps/certexi_sync/api/v1/cursor  ocs.certexi_sync.api.cursor  appinfo/routes.php:8 ocs
GET /ocs/v2.php/apps/certexi_sync/api/v1/changes  ocs.certexi_sync.api.changes  appinfo/routes.php:8 ocs
POST /ocs/v2.php/apps/certexi_sync/api/v1/tables/{tableId}/batch  ocs.certexi_sync.api.batch  appinfo/routes.php:8 ocs
The app has 3 OCS routes and no openapi.json. Clients of OCS are generated from such a specification, and nothing else tells them what these routes take and return.
